In his five full seasons in charge, Spurs were in the Premier League's top five each time - a run that has never been bettered in their history. He took the club above Arsenal for the first time in a generation and into a Champions League final for the first time ever.

Silverware was missing, much to the amusement of his critics, but the charges against Manchester City serve as a reminder that he was playing with the deck stacked against him. He overachieved and it is his thrilling football that endures in the memory.

items.title: Man City have problems - is Fernandez their most obvious?
items.excerpt: Enzo Maresca is being forced to work within an unprecedented set of circumstances this season. Up until recently, his fixation on football matters served to quieten the noise around the club. But now the anomalous nature of Manchester City'…
body: Enzo Maresca is being forced to work within an unprecedented set of circumstances this season. Up until recently, his fixation on football matters served to quieten the noise around the club. But now the anomalous nature of Manchester City's situation is apparent on and off the pitch.

Maresca began with seven straight wins in all competitions. He has since suffered a hat-trick of Premier League defeats. Concerns over performance levels in certain phases existed from the start but have come into sharper focus as results have nosedived.

Stylistically, City are far too open; just as easy to play through as play over. Only Newcastle (20) have faced more shots from fast breaks since the start of term than City's 17, conceding two goals from such situations in defeat to Nottingham Forest before the international break. body: The Premier League is back after the recent international break and the Sky Sports football writers dissect all the major talking points ahead of another busy weekend's action. Man City vs Fulham: Cottagers ideal opponents to get City back to winning ways
Are Man City in crisis heading into Saturday lunchtime's clash against Fulham, with Enzo Maresca's side having lost their previous three Premier League contests to lose top spot to Arsenal?
Those trio of reverses against Aston Villa, Brighton and, just prior to the international break, Nottingham Forest, mean City have now lost as many times as in their previous 36 league outings.

Since the start of 2007-08, though, City have only been beaten in four successive top-flight games on two occasions, in August 2008 and December 2024, and it would take a massive leap of faith to suggest Fulham are the team to inflict such ignominy on them this weekend.

items.title: The secrets of Brentford's success
items.excerpt: 'Data wizards'. 'Great recruiters'. 'Punching above their weight' - Brentford have come to be known for all these things in recent years. Now, having established themselves in the Premier League, they have become bolder about wanting to mix…
body: 'Data wizards'. 'Great recruiters'. 'Punching above their weight' - Brentford have come to be known for all these things in recent years. Now, having established themselves in the Premier League, they have become bolder about wanting to mix it with the big clubs and break into Europe.
But how do Brentford get to that next level? In their view, the answer could come via the academy.

In April, Brentford was awarded Category 1 status - the highest classification available - and their aim is to now transform into a system that is not only known for strong first-team recruitment but also one that produces academy graduates.

Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports News from under a brand-new dome being constructed to house the academy teams, sporting director Phil Giles and technical director Lee Dykes opened up about their roadmap to make Brentford one of the elites. items.title: Northern Ireland promoted to Nations League top tier with draw in Hungary
items.excerpt: Justin Devenny's superb strike saw Northern Ireland earn promotion to the top tier of the Nations League with a hard-fought 1-1 draw away to closest challengers Hungary in Budapest.
body: Justin Devenny's superb strike saw Northern Ireland earn promotion to the top tier of the Nations League with a hard-fought 1-1 draw away to closest challengers Hungary in Budapest.

Barnabas Varga ended Northern Ireland's proud record of not having conceded in this campaign when he fired the hosts in front after 35 minutes - a goal that also sent Hungary to the top of the group. How the teams lined up | Stats Nations League tables

But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for Michael O'Neill's young side, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland's one-point advantage as group leaders.

The visitors were on the back foot for much of the first half, with Hungary captain Dominik Szoboszlai hitting the post, but O'Neill, serving a touchline ban in the stands as former captain Steven Davis led things from the touchline, orchestrated key substitutions.

items.title: Mowbray steps down from Blackburn due to health issues
items.excerpt: Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues.
body: Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues.
The 62-year-old returned to football at West Brom last year following his recovery from bowel cancer, before taking charge at Blackburn in June.
In a statement, Mowbray said: "Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers.
"I'm immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I've loved working with them.
